chunks: When the messengers came to them one after the other (saying): 'Do not worship any one but God.' They said: 'If our Lord had pleased He would have sent the angels down. We reject what is sent with you.'
ai.seo_question: What was the people's argument for rejecting the prophets' message regarding the sending of angels?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological barrier of 'humanity' in prophets, where the people preferred the majesty of angels over the relatable guidance of humans, reflecting a broader theme of rejecting divine signs due to pride. The phrase 'from before them and behind them' signifies the completeness of the message, leaving no excuse for ignorance, while their dismissal underscores the common motif of attributing disbelief to the messenger's form rather than the truth of the message.
